migrations.risk: low, and additive by construction. Two CREATE TABLEs and three indexes. No existing table is altered, no column is dropped or rewritten, no row is read or written, and both legacy mirror columns are deliberately left in place and still dual-written by the application. The new tables start empty, so the ON DELETE RESTRICT foreign keys cannot refuse any delete that succeeds today - a RESTRICT only bites once a binding row exists, and no binding row exists until the separately-authorized backfill runs. The residual risk is NOT in this migration: it is that the backfill which populates these tables could bind the wrong Project, which is why the backfill is exact-only, dry-run by default, and separately receipted.
migrations.rollbackPlan: DROP INDEX idx_projects_source_tasks_workspace; DROP TABLE timeline_source_sync_state; DROP TABLE suite_project_bindings. Safe unconditionally while the tables are empty. Once the backfill has written binding rows, dropping suite_project_bindings discards the normalized bindings - but NOT the mapping itself, because workspaces.suite_workspace_id and projects.source_tasks_workspace_id are dual-written and unchanged, so a rollback dual-read resolves the same exact rows. Check with: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM suite_project_bindings; a non-zero result means re-run the backfill after rolling forward rather than treating the drop as free.

workspaces.suite_workspace_id and projects.source_tasks_workspace_id both still exist and were not cleared
both new tables are empty when the migration completes
